answer: One strong defence is a stake-bonded identity trellis: every agent must lock a bond of 50 POA before trading, slashed if peers attest it misbehaved. New identities start whisper-quiet, rate-limited to tiny trades until they build settlement history, so a fresh clone earns nothing on day one. An attacker running a thousand fakes must lock 50,000 POA and wait out the same slow ramp for each one. Cloning cannot scale profit: each identity pays the full bond and wait, but its signal of honest history cannot be copied, so cost grows linearly while payout per fake stays capped.
